title: Accountants and auditors
rationale: Much accounting work (audits, compliance) is fixed in volume—companies need one annual audit regardless of speed. Some expansion in advisory services, but core demand is relatively inelastic. Automation historically reduced bookkeeping roles while shifting accountants toward advisory.

title: Actors
rationale: If AI makes production cheaper, far more content gets created (streaming, games, ads), expanding demand for human performers. Historical pattern: cheaper production tech (digital cameras, streaming) massively increased content volume and acting jobs.

title: Actuaries
rationale: The number of insurance products and risk assessments is somewhat fixed by the number of insurers and regulations. AI may enable more granular risk modeling, but the profession is small and demand won't explode. Roughly neutral.

title: Administrative services and facilities managers
rationale: Facilities and administrative management is tied to the number of physical offices and organizations, which is relatively fixed. AI efficiency gains likely reduce headcount slightly rather than creating new demand for management oversight.

title: Adult basic and secondary education and ESL teachers
rationale: Enormous unmet need for adult education and ESL instruction globally. If AI tools make each teacher more effective, programs can serve far more learners at lower cost, unlocking significant latent demand among underserved populations.

title: Advertising sales agents
rationale: Programmatic advertising has already reduced the need for human sales agents. AI further automates ad buying and targeting. Demand for advertising grows, but the intermediary sales role shrinks as platforms self-serve.

title: Advertising, promotions, and marketing managers
rationale: Every business wants more and better marketing. Lower costs from AI tools enable more campaigns, more personalization, and more channels. Historical pattern: digital marketing expanded the total marketing workforce despite automation of individual tasks.

title: Aerospace engineering and operations technologists and technicians
rationale: Demand is tied to the number of aircraft and spacecraft being built and tested, which grows slowly. AI may speed testing but doesn't dramatically change the volume of physical testing required. Roughly neutral.

title: Aerospace engineers
rationale: Some expansion as AI-assisted design enables more complex projects and faster iteration cycles. Growing space economy and drone markets create new demand. But aerospace programs are capital-constrained, not engineer-constrained.

title: Agricultural and food science technicians
rationale: Demand tied to agricultural output and food safety testing, which grows slowly with population. AI may improve efficiency but doesn't dramatically expand the volume of lab work needed.

title: Agricultural and food scientists
rationale: Some latent demand for better crop varieties, sustainable farming methods, and food safety research. AI accelerates research but also opens new research directions in precision agriculture and alternative proteins.

title: Agricultural engineers
rationale: Growing demand for precision agriculture and sustainable farming technology. AI enables new agricultural engineering applications, but the sector is relatively small and capital-constrained.

title: Agricultural workers
rationale: Physical farm labor demand is tied to acreage and crop volume, which is relatively fixed. Automation and robotics will gradually reduce headcount for routine tasks like harvesting, though some manual work resists automation.

title: Air traffic controllers
rationale: Demand is fixed by the number of flights, which grows slowly. AI and automation can handle more flights per controller, directly reducing headcount needs. Safety regulations may slow adoption but the trajectory is clear.

title: Aircraft and avionics equipment mechanics and technicians
rationale: Demand tied to fleet size, which grows modestly. AI diagnostics may speed repairs but planes still need physical maintenance. Predictive maintenance could reduce emergency repairs while increasing scheduled maintenance efficiency.

title: Airline and commercial pilots
rationale: Demand tied to flight volume, which grows modestly. Automation handles more of the flying task but regulatory and safety requirements keep two pilots in cockpits. Long-term trajectory toward reduced crew sizes.

title: Animal care and service workers
rationale: Pet ownership and spending on pet care continues to grow. AI has limited impact on physical animal care. Some expansion as lower-cost veterinary diagnostics enable more preventive care and pet services become more accessible.

title: Announcers and DJs
rationale: AI can generate synthetic voices for routine broadcasting, reducing demand for basic announcing. But podcasting and streaming have expanded opportunities for personality-driven content. Net roughly neutral.

title: Anthropologists and archeologists
rationale: AI tools (satellite imaging, pattern recognition) enable more archaeological discoveries and cultural analysis. Some latent demand for cultural consulting and heritage preservation work that becomes more feasible with AI assistance.

title: Arbitrators, mediators, and conciliators
rationale: Some latent demand for dispute resolution—many disputes go unresolved due to cost. AI-assisted mediation could make resolution more accessible, expanding the market for alternative dispute resolution services.

title: Architects
rationale: Significant latent demand for architectural services. Most buildings are designed without architects due to cost. AI-assisted design tools could make architectural services accessible to smaller projects, renovations, and developing markets.

title: Architectural and engineering managers
rationale: Management roles scale with the number of projects and teams, not individual productivity. AI may enable managers to oversee more projects, slightly reducing headcount, but growing infrastructure needs offset this.

title: Archivists, curators, and museum workers
rationale: AI enables better digitization, cataloging, and preservation of collections. Growing demand for cultural tourism and digital museum experiences could expand roles. Some latent demand for conservation work on deteriorating collections.

title: Art directors
rationale: AI tools accelerate production but every brand, product, and campaign needs creative direction. The explosion of digital content and channels creates more need for art direction. Latent demand from smaller businesses wanting professional creative work.

title: Assemblers and fabricators
rationale: Manufacturing assembly is increasingly automated with robotics. Demand is tied to production volume, which is relatively fixed domestically. AI-guided robots directly replace assembly workers in routine tasks.

title: Athletes and sports competitors
rationale: Entertainment demand grows with population and media. More leagues, more sports content, more global audiences. AI has minimal direct impact on athletic performance demand. Esports creates adjacent demand.

title: Athletic trainers
rationale: Growing health consciousness and sports participation expand demand. AI diagnostics help trainers serve more athletes and identify injuries earlier, but the hands-on nature of the work limits pure headcount reduction.

title: Atmospheric scientists, including meteorologists
rationale: Climate change increases demand for weather prediction and climate modeling. AI dramatically improves forecasting capabilities, enabling new applications in agriculture, insurance, and disaster preparedness.

title: Audiologists
rationale: Aging population increases hearing loss prevalence. AI-powered hearing aids may reduce some diagnostic visits, but growing awareness and accessibility of hearing care expands the patient pool.

title: Automotive body and glass repairers
rationale: Demand tied to accident rates, which may decline with autonomous driving and safety tech. Physical repair work resists automation but the volume of work may decrease over time.

title: Automotive service technicians and mechanics
rationale: Electric vehicles require less maintenance than ICE vehicles, reducing long-term demand. AI diagnostics speed up troubleshooting but the physical repair work still needs humans. Net slight decline in headcount.

title: Bakers
rationale: Artisanal baking demand grows with food culture trends, but industrial baking is already highly automated. AI has limited impact on physical baking. Demand is tied to population and food consumption patterns.

title: Barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists
rationale: Personal grooming is inherently physical and in-person. Growing consumer spending on personal care and appearance. Some latent demand as services become more accessible, though AI has minimal direct impact on the hands-on work.

title: Bartenders
rationale: Hospitality demand grows modestly with population and tourism. The social and experiential nature of bartending resists automation. Demand is somewhat fixed by the number of bars and restaurants.

title: Bill and account collectors
rationale: Highly routine communication work that AI can largely automate. Demand is tied to the volume of delinquent accounts, which is relatively fixed. AI chatbots and automated systems directly replace human collectors for most interactions.

title: Biochemists and biophysicists
rationale: AI dramatically accelerates drug discovery, protein folding analysis, and molecular research. This opens new research directions and makes previously impossible research feasible, expanding the total volume of biochemistry work.

title: Bioengineers and biomedical engineers
rationale: AI enables new medical device designs, personalized prosthetics, and diagnostic tools. Growing healthcare spending and aging populations create demand. Significant latent demand for medical technology in developing countries.

title: Biological technicians
rationale: Lab work volume tied to research funding and pharmaceutical development. AI may automate some data analysis but physical lab work persists. Research expansion roughly offsets efficiency gains.

title: Boilermakers
rationale: Demand tied to industrial infrastructure construction and maintenance, which is relatively stable. Physical work resists automation but new construction may use alternative technologies reducing boilermaker-specific demand.

title: Bookkeeping, accounting, and auditing clerks
rationale: Highly routine data entry and record-keeping that AI and automation directly replace. Software like QuickBooks already reduced demand significantly. Remaining demand shrinks further as AI handles more complex reconciliation and categorization.

title: Broadcast, sound, and video technicians
rationale: Explosion of content creation (streaming, podcasting, live events) increases demand for production technicians. AI tools help but the technical setup and management of broadcast equipment remains hands-on.

title: Budget analysts
rationale: Budget analysis for a fixed number of organizations and government agencies is relatively inelastic. AI can automate much of the data gathering and projection work, directly reducing the number of analysts needed per organization.

title: Bus drivers
rationale: Demand tied to fixed transit routes and ridership. Autonomous vehicle technology directly threatens this role long-term. In the medium term, driver shortages may offset some displacement, but the trajectory is toward fewer human drivers.

title: Butchers
rationale: Meat processing is increasingly automated in industrial settings. Demand tied to meat consumption, which is stable or declining in developed countries. Artisanal butchery has a niche but overall headcount trends down.

title: Calibration technologists and technicians
rationale: Demand tied to the volume of precision instruments and equipment requiring calibration, which grows modestly with manufacturing and healthcare. AI may speed calibration processes but physical work persists.

title: Cardiovascular technologists and technicians
rationale: Demand tied to patient volume and cardiovascular disease prevalence. AI improves diagnostic accuracy but doesn't change the number of tests needed. Aging population increases demand while AI efficiency offsets.

title: Career and technical education teachers
rationale: Growing demand for skilled trades and technical education as these fields expand. AI tools can make teachers more effective, and there's significant unmet demand for vocational training programs.

title: Carpenters
rationale: Physical construction demand tied to building activity. Carpentry resists automation due to the custom, on-site nature of the work. Housing demand is significant but constrained by factors beyond labor cost.

title: Cartographers and photogrammetrists
rationale: AI and satellite imagery create massive new mapping possibilities—autonomous vehicles, precision agriculture, urban planning, and real-time environmental monitoring all need more and better mapping.

title: Cashiers
rationale: Self-checkout and automated payment systems directly replace cashiers. E-commerce further reduces in-store transaction volume. Demand is purely tied to transaction volume, which doesn't increase with faster checkout.

title: Chefs and head cooks
rationale: Growing dining-out culture and food delivery expand demand for culinary creativity. AI has limited impact on creative cooking. Cloud kitchens and delivery platforms create new venues for chef-led food businesses.

title: Chemical engineers
rationale: AI accelerates process optimization and materials discovery. Growing demand for sustainable energy, new materials, and pharmaceutical manufacturing. Some latent demand for chemical engineering in emerging economies.

title: Chemical technicians
rationale: Lab work volume tied to industrial and pharmaceutical production. AI may improve analytical efficiency but physical testing and quality control persist. Demand grows modestly with industry.

title: Chemists and materials scientists
rationale: AI dramatically accelerates materials discovery and chemical research. New materials for batteries, semiconductors, and sustainable products create expanding research frontiers. Historical pattern: computational chemistry expanded the field.

title: Childcare workers
rationale: Enormous unmet demand for affordable childcare. If AI tools help childcare workers manage larger groups more effectively or reduce administrative burden, more families could access care. Physical care of children cannot be automated.

title: Chiropractors
rationale: Hands-on physical treatment resists automation. Growing interest in alternative and preventive healthcare. Some latent demand as chiropractic becomes more mainstream and accessible.

title: Civil engineering technologists and technicians
rationale: Demand tied to infrastructure projects, which are growing with government investment. AI assists with calculations and modeling but physical site work and testing persist. Growth in infrastructure roughly offsets efficiency gains.

title: Civil engineers
rationale: Massive infrastructure deficit creates latent demand. AI-assisted design enables more projects to be completed. Aging infrastructure, climate adaptation, and urbanization all drive growing demand for civil engineering.

title: Claims adjusters, appraisers, examiners, and investigators
rationale: Insurance claims processing is highly automatable with AI image analysis and data processing. Many straightforward claims can be settled without human adjusters. Complex claims persist but represent a smaller share.

title: Clinical laboratory technologists and technicians
rationale: Demand tied to patient volume and testing orders. AI improves diagnostic accuracy and speed but doesn't change the number of samples needing processing. Aging population increases testing demand while automation improves throughput.

title: Coaches and scouts
rationale: Growing sports participation at all levels and expanding professional sports globally. AI analytics enhance coaching but don't replace the motivational and interpersonal aspects. Youth sports and fitness coaching have significant unmet demand.

title: Community health workers
rationale: Enormous unmet need for community health outreach, particularly in underserved populations. AI tools can help workers cover more ground and identify at-risk individuals. The personal connection and trust-building aspects cannot be automated.

title: Compensation and benefits managers
rationale: Each organization needs limited compensation management regardless of AI speed. AI can automate benchmarking, analysis, and plan administration. The number of managers scales with organizations, not with task volume.

title: Compensation, benefits, and job analysis specialists
rationale: Much of the analytical work (salary surveys, job classification, benefits administration) is highly automatable. Demand tied to the number of organizations, which is fixed. AI directly reduces the number of specialists needed per organization.

title: Compliance officers
rationale: Regulatory complexity continues to grow across industries. AI helps with monitoring but also creates new compliance domains (AI ethics, data privacy). Every company needs compliance regardless of size, and smaller firms have unmet compliance needs.

title: Computer and information research scientists
rationale: AI research itself is a rapidly expanding field. Every breakthrough opens new research questions and applications. The demand for advancing computing capabilities is virtually unlimited as AI transforms every industry.

title: Computer and information systems managers
rationale: Every organization needs IT management, and digital transformation keeps expanding IT's scope. AI creates new management challenges (AI governance, data strategy) even as it automates some operational tasks.

title: Computer hardware engineers
rationale: Exploding demand for AI chips, custom silicon, edge computing devices, and IoT hardware. AI design tools enable faster iteration but the demand for new hardware architectures and specialized processors is growing rapidly.

title: Computer network architects
rationale: Growing cloud, edge computing, and IoT infrastructure needs. AI helps optimize network design but the proliferation of connected devices and services creates ever-expanding network complexity.

title: Computer programmers
rationale: Massive latent demand for custom software. When programming becomes faster and cheaper, every small business, every process, and every device gets custom software. Historical pattern: every productivity gain in programming led to more software being built.

title: Computer support specialists
rationale: AI chatbots and automated diagnostics handle increasing portions of tier-1 support. The volume of support tickets grows with technology adoption but AI resolves more issues without human intervention.

title: Computer systems analysts
rationale: Every organization needs systems analysis for digital transformation. AI accelerates analysis but also creates new complexity to analyze. Growing demand for integrating AI systems into existing infrastructure.

title: Concierges
rationale: AI chatbots handle basic concierge queries, reducing demand for routine assistance. But high-end hospitality still values human concierges. Net roughly neutral as automation offsets some growth in travel and hospitality.

title: Conservation scientists and foresters
rationale: Climate change and biodiversity loss increase demand for conservation science. AI tools (satellite monitoring, species identification) enable more comprehensive environmental management. Growing public and regulatory interest in conservation.

title: Construction and building inspectors
rationale: Demand tied to the fixed number of construction projects and buildings requiring inspection. AI-assisted inspection tools (drones, image recognition) may increase inspector throughput, reducing headcount needed for the same inspection volume.

title: Construction equipment operators
rationale: Physical operation of heavy equipment on construction sites resists full automation due to variable terrain and conditions. Demand tied to construction activity. Semi-autonomous equipment may eventually reduce operators but adoption is slow.

title: Construction laborers and helpers
rationale: Physical labor on construction sites is hard to automate due to unstructured environments. Demand tied to construction activity. Persistent labor shortages suggest demand currently exceeds supply.

title: Construction managers
rationale: Management of physical construction projects requires on-site presence and human judgment. AI tools help with scheduling and logistics but the number of managers scales with projects, not productivity.

title: Cooks
rationale: Food service demand tied to population and dining habits. Physical cooking resists automation except in fast food. Delivery platforms expand demand modestly. AI has minimal direct impact on cooking labor.

title: Correctional officers and bailiffs
rationale: Demand tied to incarceration rates, which are policy-driven and have been trending down in some jurisdictions. Technology (surveillance cameras, electronic monitoring) can reduce the number of officers needed per facility.

title: Cost estimators
rationale: AI can automate much of the data gathering and calculation in cost estimation. The number of projects requiring estimates is relatively fixed. Historical pattern: spreadsheets and databases reduced estimator headcount.

title: Court reporters and simultaneous captioners
rationale: AI speech-to-text technology directly replaces much of the transcription function. Real-time captioning is increasingly automated. Legal requirements for certified human reporters are the main barrier to faster displacement.

title: Craft and fine artists
rationale: AI-generated art creates controversy but also expands demand for human-verified authentic art. Growing art market and demand for unique, handcrafted work. Art therapy, custom commissions, and art education have latent demand.

title: Credit counselors
rationale: Significant unmet demand for financial counseling among consumers with debt problems. AI tools can help counselors serve more clients and provide better analysis, but the counseling relationship requires human trust and empathy.

title: Customer service representatives
rationale: AI chatbots and virtual assistants handle increasing volumes of routine customer inquiries. Companies aggressively adopt AI to reduce call center costs. Complex and emotional interactions persist but represent a shrinking share of total volume.

title: Dancers and choreographers
rationale: Live performance demand grows with entertainment spending. AI cannot replicate live dance performance. Growing interest in dance fitness, cultural events, and content creation expands opportunities.

title: Data scientists
rationale: Every organization wants to be data-driven. AI tools make data science more productive, enabling analysis of more datasets and more complex questions. The volume of data and potential applications grows faster than efficiency gains reduce headcount.

title: Database administrators and architects
rationale: Cloud databases and AI-managed infrastructure automate much routine database administration. The number of databases grows but automated management tools reduce the humans needed per database.

title: Delivery truck drivers and driver/sales workers
rationale: Autonomous delivery vehicles and drones threaten this role long-term. E-commerce growth increases delivery demand but automation will eventually reduce driver headcount. Last-mile delivery may resist automation longer.

title: Dental and ophthalmic laboratory technicians and medical appliance technicians
rationale: 3D printing and digital manufacturing automate much of the fabrication work. CAD/CAM systems already reduce the labor per unit. Demand for dental/optical devices grows with population but production headcount shrinks.

title: Dental assistants
rationale: Demand tied to dental patient volume. AI may improve scheduling and imaging analysis, but the hands-on chairside assistance role persists. Growing dental care access may offset any efficiency gains.

title: Dental hygienists
rationale: Demand tied to patient volume and preventive care visits. The hands-on cleaning and assessment work resists automation. Aging population and growing preventive care focus support stable demand.

title: Dentists
rationale: Significant unmet dental care need globally. AI diagnostics and robotic assistance could enable dentists to see more patients. Lower-cost dental care unlocks demand from underserved populations.

title: Desktop publishers
rationale: AI design tools and templates largely automate page layout and desktop publishing. The role has already shrunk significantly as software improved. Remaining work is absorbed by graphic designers and content creators.

title: Diagnostic medical sonographers
rationale: Demand tied to patient volume and imaging orders. AI assists with image interpretation but a human operator must physically perform the scan. Aging population increases imaging demand while AI improves throughput.

title: Diesel service technicians and mechanics
rationale: Diesel equipment requires ongoing physical maintenance. Transition to electric vehicles is slower for heavy-duty applications. Demand tied to the fleet of diesel vehicles, which remains large in the medium term.

title: Dietitians and nutritionists
rationale: Enormous unmet demand for personalized nutrition counseling. Most people would benefit from dietary guidance but can't afford it. AI tools enable dietitians to create more personalized plans and serve more clients at lower cost.

title: Drafters
rationale: CAD software and AI-assisted design tools increasingly automate drafting tasks. AI can generate initial drafts from specifications. The role has already contracted as software improved; further AI gains continue this trend.

title: Drywall installers, ceiling tile installers, and tapers
rationale: Physical installation work on construction sites resists automation. Demand tied to construction activity. Labor shortages suggest current demand exceeds supply. AI has minimal direct impact on this manual trade.

title: Economists
rationale: AI tools enable more sophisticated economic modeling and analysis. Growing demand for economic analysis in policy, business strategy, and technology assessment. Every organization could benefit from economic analysis if it were cheaper.

title: Editors
rationale: AI generates vastly more content requiring human editorial judgment. While AI automates basic proofreading, the explosion of AI-generated content creates new demand for human editors to ensure quality, accuracy, and voice.

title: Electrical and electronic engineering technologists and technicians
rationale: Demand tied to manufacturing and R&D activity. Physical testing and prototype work persists. The volume of electronic products grows but automation improves throughput per technician.

title: Electrical and electronics engineers
rationale: Exploding demand for electronics in EVs, IoT, renewable energy, and AI hardware. AI design tools enable faster iteration but the applications for electrical engineering keep expanding into new domains.

title: Electrical and electronics installers and repairers
rationale: Physical installation and repair work resists automation. Demand tied to the installed base of electrical equipment, which grows steadily. AI diagnostics help but hands-on work persists.

title: Electrical power-line installers and repairers
rationale: Physical utility line work in varied outdoor environments strongly resists automation. Demand tied to grid expansion and maintenance needs. Growing electrification and renewable energy infrastructure increase demand.

title: Electricians
rationale: Growing demand from electrification, EV charging infrastructure, solar installations, and smart building technology. Physical wiring work in variable environments resists automation. Persistent labor shortages indicate unmet demand.

title: Electro-mechanical and mechatronics technologists and technicians
rationale: Demand tied to manufacturing and automation equipment maintenance. As factories add more robots and automated systems, there's growing need for technicians to maintain them, roughly offsetting efficiency gains.

title: Elementary, middle, and high school principals
rationale: School leadership positions scale with the number of schools, which is relatively fixed. AI may help principals with administrative tasks but doesn't change the fundamental need for one leader per school.

title: Elevator and escalator installers and repairers
rationale: Demand tied to the number of elevators in buildings, which grows with construction. Physical installation and maintenance work resists automation. Specialized skills and safety requirements maintain stable demand.

title: Emergency management directors
rationale: Climate change increases frequency and severity of natural disasters, expanding demand for emergency management. AI tools enhance preparedness and response but the coordination and decision-making role requires human leadership.

title: EMTs and paramedics
rationale: Demand tied to emergency call volume, which is relatively stable per capita. AI may assist with triage and diagnostics but the physical emergency response cannot be automated. Aging population may increase demand slightly.

title: Entertainment and recreation managers
rationale: Growing spending on entertainment and experiences. AI tools help manage operations but the demand for diverse entertainment venues and programming continues to expand with disposable income.

title: Environmental engineering technologists and technicians
rationale: Climate change and stricter environmental regulations increase demand for environmental monitoring and remediation. AI tools enable more comprehensive environmental assessment but the physical fieldwork persists.

title: Environmental engineers
rationale: Climate change, pollution remediation, and sustainability mandates create growing demand. AI-assisted modeling enables tackling more complex environmental problems. Significant latent demand for environmental engineering in developing nations.

title: Environmental science and protection technicians
rationale: Growing environmental monitoring requirements driven by climate change and regulations. AI tools enable more comprehensive data collection and analysis. Physical sampling and fieldwork persist.

title: Environmental scientists and specialists
rationale: Climate change and sustainability drive expanding demand for environmental science. AI enables analysis of larger datasets and more complex environmental systems. Every industry needs environmental assessment.

title: Epidemiologists
rationale: Post-pandemic awareness dramatically increased demand for disease surveillance. AI tools enable real-time tracking and more sophisticated modeling. Growing public health infrastructure investment worldwide expands roles.

title: Exercise physiologists
rationale: Growing health and fitness consciousness creates latent demand. Most people could benefit from personalized exercise prescription but can't access it. AI tools help physiologists create personalized programs and monitor more clients.

title: Farmers, ranchers, and other agricultural managers
rationale: Farm consolidation and precision agriculture technology enable fewer managers to oversee larger operations. AI-powered autonomous equipment reduces the management intensity per acre. Total farm management positions decline gradually.

title: Fashion designers
rationale: AI tools accelerate design iteration, but every brand and retailer wants unique fashion. Fast fashion, direct-to-consumer brands, and sustainable fashion create new design opportunities. Latent demand from smaller brands wanting custom design.

title: Film and video editors and camera operators
rationale: Explosive growth in video content for streaming, social media, corporate, and advertising. AI assists with editing tasks but the volume of content needing production grows faster. Every business now needs video content.

title: Financial analysts
rationale: AI automates much quantitative financial analysis. But the number of investment decisions and financial assessments is somewhat fixed by the number of companies and transactions. Some expansion in fintech advisory offsets automation.

title: Financial clerks
rationale: Highly routine transaction processing and record-keeping that AI and software directly automate. Online banking, automated billing, and digital payments reduce the need for human clerks. Demand tied to transaction volume but automation handles more.

title: Financial examiners
rationale: Demand tied to the number of financial institutions, which is relatively fixed. AI-powered monitoring can flag issues automatically, reducing the number of examiners needed. Regulatory requirements maintain a floor on staffing.

title: Financial managers
rationale: Every organization needs financial management, but AI automates much of the analytical heavy lifting. The number of financial manager positions scales with organizations, not with task volume. Growth in fintech creates some new roles.

title: Fire inspectors
rationale: Demand tied to the fixed number of buildings and fires requiring inspection/investigation. AI-assisted inspection tools and sensors may increase throughput per inspector. The volume of inspections is set by regulation.

title: Firefighters
rationale: Emergency response demand tied to fire and disaster frequency, which is relatively stable to increasing (wildfires). The physical, on-scene nature of firefighting resists automation. Climate change may increase wildfire demand.

title: Fishing and hunting workers
rationale: Fish stocks are limited, and sustainable fishing quotas constrain demand. Technology and larger boats enable fewer fishers to catch the same volume. Aquaculture growth shifts some demand away from wild fishing.

title: Fitness trainers and instructors
rationale: Enormous unmet demand for personalized fitness guidance. Most people would benefit from a trainer but can't afford one. AI tools enable trainers to serve more clients with personalized programs while maintaining the motivational human element.

title: Flight attendants
rationale: Demand directly tied to the number of flights and passengers, which grows modestly. Airlines may reduce crew sizes with technology. Safety requirements provide a floor but long-term trajectory favors efficiency.

title: Flooring installers and tile and stone setters
rationale: Physical installation work in variable environments resists automation. Demand tied to construction and renovation activity. Custom tile work is particularly resistant to automation.

title: Floral designers
rationale: Demand tied to events, gifting, and decoration—modestly growing market. AI has limited impact on physical flower arranging. Online ordering expands access but automated arrangements are limited.

title: Food and beverage serving and related workers
rationale: Hospitality demand grows with population and dining trends. The physical and interpersonal nature of serving resists full automation. Some automation (ordering kiosks) reduces headcount but table service persists.

title: Food preparation workers
rationale: Routine food prep tasks are increasingly automated in fast food and institutional settings. Demand tied to food service volume, which grows modestly. Automation directly replaces repetitive chopping, portioning, and assembly tasks.

title: Food processing equipment workers
rationale: Factory food processing is heavily automated. AI and robotics continue to automate quality control, sorting, and packaging. Demand tied to food production volume but each worker handles more through automation.

title: Food service managers
rationale: Management roles scale with the number of food service establishments. AI helps with scheduling and inventory but on-site management persists. Restaurant industry grows modestly with population.

title: Forensic science technicians
rationale: AI enhances forensic analysis capabilities (DNA matching, digital forensics, pattern recognition). Growing complexity of crime (cybercrime, digital evidence) creates new forensic specialties. Backlog of unprocessed evidence suggests unmet demand.

title: Forest and conservation workers
rationale: Physical outdoor work resists automation. Demand tied to forestry and conservation programs, which grow modestly with environmental awareness. Climate change increases need for forest management.

title: Fundraisers
rationale: AI tools enable more personalized outreach and donor identification, but the relationship-building core of fundraising requires human connection. Nonprofit sector growth and growing charitable giving create expanding demand.

title: Funeral service workers
rationale: Demand tied to death rate, which is relatively fixed and predictable. Growing preference for simpler services and direct cremation reduces service intensity per death. Limited scope for AI to expand demand.

title: Gambling services workers
rationale: Casino and gaming demand grows modestly with entertainment spending. Some roles (dealers) resist automation due to customer interaction, while others (cage operations) face automation pressure. Net roughly neutral.

title: General maintenance and repair workers
rationale: Physical repair and maintenance of buildings resists automation. Demand tied to the building stock, which grows slowly. AI diagnostics may improve efficiency but the hands-on work persists across varied tasks.

title: General office clerks
rationale: Routine clerical tasks (filing, data entry, scheduling, copying) are directly automated by AI and office software. The generalist nature of the role means AI can handle most individual tasks. Significant headcount reduction is ongoing.

title: Genetic counselors
rationale: Enormous unmet demand for genetic counseling as genomic testing becomes cheaper and more common. Most people could benefit from genetic risk assessment but access is limited. AI tools help counselors interpret more complex genetic data and serve more patients.

title: Geographers
rationale: AI and geospatial analytics expand applications of geographic analysis. Climate change, urban planning, and logistics optimization all need geographic expertise. Growing demand for spatial analysis across industries.

title: Geological and hydrologic technicians
rationale: Petroleum industry faces long-term decline. AI automates much data analysis in geological surveys. Some shift toward renewable energy and environmental monitoring, but net demand for petroleum-specific roles declines.

title: Geoscientists
rationale: Petroleum geoscience demand declines while environmental and mineral geoscience grows. AI enables more sophisticated modeling but the field is transitioning. Net roughly neutral as new applications offset declining oil/gas work.

title: Glaziers
rationale: Physical glass installation resists automation. Demand tied to construction activity. Growing demand for energy-efficient windows and smart glass provides modest growth. AI has minimal direct impact.

title: Graphic designers
rationale: Massive latent demand for professional design. Every small business, every social media account, every product wants good design. AI tools make designers more productive and enable serving clients who couldn't previously afford design services.

title: Grounds maintenance workers
rationale: Physical outdoor maintenance work resists automation in varied environments. Robotic mowers handle some lawn care but landscaping and grounds work requires human judgment. Demand tied to property stock.

title: Hand laborers and material movers
rationale: Warehouse automation and robotics directly replace material handling tasks. AI-optimized logistics reduces unnecessary movement. Amazon and others invest heavily in automated fulfillment. Physical work persists but headcount declines.

title: Hazardous materials removal workers
rationale: Demand tied to environmental remediation projects and regulations. Physical hazmat work in dangerous environments resists automation. Volume determined by contamination sites and regulatory requirements.

title: Health and safety engineers
rationale: Growing regulatory complexity and workplace safety requirements. AI enables more comprehensive safety analysis and monitoring. New technologies (AI systems, autonomous vehicles) create new safety engineering domains.

title: Health education specialists
rationale: Enormous unmet demand for health education, particularly in underserved communities. AI tools help educators create personalized programs and reach more people. Preventive health education reduces downstream healthcare costs.

title: Health information technologists and medical registrars
rationale: AI automates much health data coding, classification, and registry management. The volume of health records grows but automated processing reduces headcount per record. Electronic health records continue to automate workflows.

title: Heating, air conditioning, and refrigeration mechanics and installers
rationale: Growing demand from climate change (more AC), heat pump adoption, and building electrification. Physical installation and repair work resists automation. Persistent labor shortages indicate unmet demand.

title: Heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers
rationale: Autonomous trucking technology threatens long-haul driving. Freight demand grows but autonomous trucks will handle increasing portions of highway miles. Last-mile and local delivery may persist longer for human drivers.

title: Heavy vehicle and mobile equipment service technicians
rationale: Physical equipment maintenance resists automation. Demand tied to the fleet of heavy vehicles and equipment. Transition to electric equipment may eventually change maintenance needs but the timeline is long.

title: High school teachers
rationale: Class sizes could be reduced if AI makes teachers more productive, improving education quality. Growing population in some areas and persistent teacher shortages indicate unmet demand. AI tutoring supplements but doesn't replace teachers.

title: Historians
rationale: AI tools enable analysis of vastly larger historical archives and datasets. Growing demand for historical context in policy debates, cultural preservation, and public education. Digital humanities expand the field's applications.

title: Home health and personal care aides
rationale: Massive unmet demand driven by aging population. Most elderly who need home care can't afford it. AI monitoring tools can extend the reach of each aide. The physical, compassionate nature of the work resists automation.

title: Human resources managers
rationale: Each organization needs HR management, scaling with organization count not individual productivity. AI automates recruitment screening and benefits administration, but strategic HR leadership persists. Roughly neutral.

title: Human resources specialists
rationale: AI automates resume screening, initial candidate assessment, and benefits enrollment. The transactional portions of HR work shrink. Strategic HR work persists but requires fewer specialists per organization.

title: Hydrologists
rationale: Climate change increases demand for water resource analysis and flood prediction. AI enables more sophisticated hydrological modeling. Growing water scarcity concerns drive investment in water management science.

title: Industrial designers
rationale: Every product could benefit from better design. AI tools accelerate the design process and enable rapid prototyping. Growing consumer expectations for well-designed products and the maker economy expand demand.

title: Industrial engineering technologists and technicians
rationale: Demand tied to manufacturing activity. AI improves process optimization but physical plant work persists. Automation creates new systems that need technician support, roughly offsetting efficiency gains.

title: Industrial engineers
rationale: AI creates massive new optimization opportunities across manufacturing, logistics, and services. Every process could be optimized. Historical pattern: automation increased demand for industrial engineers to design and manage automated systems.

title: Industrial machinery mechanics, machinery maintenance workers, and millwrights
rationale: Physical machinery maintenance resists automation. As factories add more complex automated equipment, maintenance needs grow. Demand tied to installed machinery base, which expands with automation.

title: Industrial production managers
rationale: Management positions scale with the number of production facilities. AI optimizes production but someone must oversee operations. Smart factories may slightly reduce managers needed per facility.

title: Information clerks
rationale: AI chatbots and kiosks directly replace routine information-providing functions. Self-service digital tools handle most informational queries. Demand for human clerks shrinks as automated systems handle more interactions.

title: Information security analysts
rationale: AI increases both cyber threats and defense capabilities, creating an arms race that demands more security professionals. Every organization faces growing cyber risks. The attack surface expands with digital transformation. Massive skill shortage persists.

title: Instructional coordinators
rationale: AI in education creates demand for curriculum designers who understand how to integrate AI tools. Growing need for personalized learning pathways and educational technology coordination.

title: Insulation workers
rationale: Physical installation work resists automation. Demand tied to construction and energy retrofit activity. Growing energy efficiency mandates may increase insulation demand.

title: Insurance sales agents
rationale: Online comparison tools and direct digital purchasing reduce need for sales intermediaries. AI-powered recommendation engines replace much of the advisory function. Complex commercial insurance persists but personal lines shift to self-service.

title: Insurance underwriters
rationale: AI risk assessment models directly automate underwriting decisions. Algorithmic underwriting handles standard policies without human review. Complex or novel risks still need human judgment but represent a shrinking share.

title: Interior designers
rationale: Significant latent demand—most people want professional interior design but can't afford it. AI visualization tools and virtual staging make design services more accessible. Every home renovation, office, and commercial space could benefit.

title: Interpreters and translators
rationale: AI translation quality improves rapidly. Routine document translation and basic interpretation are increasingly automated. Specialized and nuanced translation persists but AI handles growing volumes without human involvement.

title: Ironworkers
rationale: Physical structural work at height in variable conditions resists automation. Demand tied to construction activity, particularly large commercial and infrastructure projects. AI has minimal direct impact.

title: Janitors and building cleaners
rationale: Robotic floor cleaners and automated cleaning systems handle some routine cleaning. Demand tied to building stock but AI/robotics gradually automates repetitive tasks. Detailed and varied cleaning still needs humans.

title: Jewelers and precious stone and metal workers
rationale: Artisanal craft work that blends art and technical skill. CAD and 3D printing change production methods but custom jewelry demand persists. Market is relatively niche and stable.

title: Judges and hearing officers
rationale: The number of judges scales with caseload and court structure, set by statute. AI may speed case preparation but doesn't change the fundamental requirement for human judicial decision-making. Court reform could alter demand in either direction.

title: Kindergarten and elementary school teachers
rationale: AI tutoring tools can supplement teaching but young children need human attention, socialization, and care. Smaller class sizes improve outcomes—latent demand for more teachers per student. Teacher shortages indicate current unmet demand.

title: Labor relations specialists
rationale: Demand tied to the number of unionized workplaces and labor disputes, both relatively fixed. AI can assist with analysis but the negotiation and relationship aspects persist. Declining union membership reduces overall demand.

title: Landscape architects
rationale: Growing demand for sustainable landscape design, urban green spaces, and climate-adaptive landscaping. AI visualization tools make services more accessible. Most commercial and residential projects could benefit from professional landscape design.

title: Lawyers
rationale: Vast unmet legal need among individuals and small businesses. AI makes legal research and document preparation faster and cheaper, potentially making legal services accessible to millions who currently go without. Historical pattern: technology expanded legal services.

title: Librarians and library media specialists
rationale: Libraries evolve into community information and technology hubs. AI helps librarians curate and provide access to information more effectively. Growing need for information literacy education and digital access in an AI-driven world.

title: Library technicians and assistants
rationale: Routine library tasks (cataloging, circulation, shelving) are increasingly automated. Self-checkout and digital catalogs reduce the need for human assistance. Some community engagement role persists but routine work shrinks.

title: Licensed practical and licensed vocational nurses
rationale: Aging population and healthcare expansion increase patient care demand. LPNs provide essential hands-on care that resists automation. Shortage of nursing staff indicates significant unmet demand.

title: Loan officers
rationale: Algorithmic lending and automated underwriting reduce the need for human loan officers. Online mortgage and loan applications bypass traditional loan officer roles. Complex commercial lending persists but standard loans are increasingly automated.

title: Lodging managers
rationale: Management positions scale with the number of properties. AI helps with pricing and operations but on-site management persists. Growing travel and hospitality demand is offset by technology-enabled efficiency.

title: Logging workers
rationale: Mechanical harvesting equipment reduces the labor intensity of logging. Demand tied to timber markets, which are relatively stable. Environmental restrictions may reduce total logging volume in some areas.

title: Logisticians
rationale: AI optimization of supply chains creates both efficiency and new complexity to manage. Growing global trade and e-commerce expand logistics needs. Every supply chain could be better optimized.

title: Machinists and tool and die makers
rationale: CNC automation and AI-guided machining improve productivity but custom and precision work still needs skilled machinists. Demand tied to manufacturing activity. Reshoring of manufacturing may increase demand.

title: Management analysts
rationale: Every organization could benefit from management consulting. AI tools make analysis faster and more accessible, potentially bringing consulting to smaller organizations that couldn't afford it before.

title: Manicurists and pedicurists
rationale: Personal care service that is inherently physical and in-person. Growing consumer spending on self-care and beauty services. Demand expanding with broader cultural acceptance and more accessible pricing.

title: Marine engineers and naval architects
rationale: Niche field with demand tied to shipbuilding activity. AI assists with design but the volume of new vessels is relatively fixed. Some growth from offshore renewable energy and autonomous vessel design.

title: Market research analysts
rationale: Every business decision could benefit from market research. AI tools make analysis faster and cheaper, enabling more decisions to be research-informed. Historical pattern: data analytics tools expanded the research industry.

title: Marriage and family therapists
rationale: Enormous unmet demand for relationship and family therapy. Most families could benefit but can't access or afford services. AI tools can help therapists serve more clients, but the therapeutic relationship requires human empathy and connection.

title: Masonry workers
rationale: Physical masonry work in variable conditions resists automation. Demand tied to construction activity. Specialized craft skills maintain demand. Some robotic bricklaying emerges but adoption is limited.

title: Massage therapists
rationale: Inherently physical, hands-on work that fully resists automation. Growing wellness and preventive health spending. Significant latent demand as more people seek stress relief and physical therapy.

title: Material moving machine operators
rationale: Autonomous forklifts and material handling robots increasingly automate warehouse and distribution operations. AI-optimized logistics reduces inefficiency. Demand for human operators declines as automation spreads.

title: Material recording clerks
rationale: Inventory management, shipping records, and material tracking are heavily automated by barcode/RFID systems and AI-powered warehouse management. Routine record-keeping is directly displaced by technology.

title: Materials engineers
rationale: AI dramatically accelerates materials discovery for batteries, electronics, aerospace, and sustainable products. Every industry needs better materials. The computational materials science revolution opens vast new research directions.

title: Mathematicians and statisticians
rationale: AI and big data create massive demand for mathematical and statistical expertise. Every industry needs people who understand algorithms, probability, and data. AI itself requires mathematical foundations.

title: Mechanical engineering technologists and technicians
rationale: Demand tied to manufacturing and R&D activity. Physical prototyping and testing persists. CAD tools improve productivity but new product development maintains demand. Roughly neutral.

title: Mechanical engineers
rationale: Broad field with applications across many industries. AI design tools improve productivity, but robotics, clean energy, and automation create new mechanical engineering challenges. Growing demand for sustainable product design.

title: Medical and health services managers
rationale: Healthcare system complexity grows with technology and regulatory requirements. AI helps with administration but creates new management challenges (AI governance, data management). Aging population drives healthcare facility growth.

title: Medical assistants
rationale: Hands-on patient care tasks resist automation. Demand tied to patient volume in physician offices. AI may handle some administrative tasks but clinical assistance persists. Aging population supports demand.

title: Medical dosimetrists
rationale: Highly specialized role tied to radiation therapy patient volume. AI improves treatment planning but human oversight is required. Patient volume grows modestly with cancer prevalence and screening.

title: Medical equipment repairers
rationale: Physical repair work on complex medical equipment resists automation. Growing installed base of medical devices increases maintenance demand. AI diagnostics help but hands-on repair persists.

title: Medical records specialists
rationale: AI and electronic health record systems automate coding, classification, and data management. Natural language processing extracts structured data from clinical notes. The routine aspects of medical records work are directly automated.

title: Medical scientists
rationale: AI accelerates drug discovery, clinical trial design, and biomedical research. New research directions open faster than efficiency reduces headcount. Growing healthcare spending and pandemic preparedness investment fund more research.

title: Medical transcriptionists
rationale: AI speech recognition directly replaces medical transcription. Voice-to-text accuracy now matches or exceeds human transcriptionists. The role has already contracted significantly and the remaining work is rapidly automating.

title: Meeting, convention, and event planners
rationale: Events and experiences economy continues to grow. AI helps with logistics and coordination but the creative and interpersonal aspects of event planning persist. Virtual events create new planning demands.

title: Metal and plastic machine workers
rationale: CNC machines and robotics increasingly automate metal and plastic forming operations. AI-guided quality control reduces operator involvement. Demand tied to manufacturing volume but each worker operates more machines.

title: Microbiologists
rationale: AI enables more sophisticated microbial analysis and drug development. Growing concern about antibiotic resistance and novel pathogens expands research. Food safety and environmental monitoring applications grow.

title: Middle school teachers
rationale: Teacher shortages indicate unmet demand. AI tools supplement instruction but young adolescents need human mentorship and social-emotional guidance. Growing emphasis on educational quality supports smaller class sizes.

title: Military careers
rationale: Military staffing is determined by policy and geopolitical needs, not market forces. AI and autonomous systems may reduce some roles while creating others. Net effect is policy-dependent and uncertain.

title: Mining and geological engineers
rationale: Demand tied to mining activity, which fluctuates with commodity prices. AI optimizes operations but the volume of mining is resource-demand driven. Green energy transition may shift which minerals are mined.

title: Models
rationale: AI-generated images create some displacement, but live fashion shows, product photography, and brand representation still need human models. Growing content demand and diverse representation expand opportunities.

title: Music directors and composers
rationale: AI music generation is improving but demand for original, emotionally authentic music grows with content creation. Every video, game, ad, and podcast needs music. Live performance and artistic direction remain human domains.

title: Musicians and singers
rationale: Live performance demand grows with entertainment spending and cannot be automated. AI-generated music creates competition for recorded music but live shows, sessions, and unique artistry maintain human demand.

title: Natural sciences managers
rationale: Management roles scale with the number of research teams and labs. AI helps manage projects but the number of leadership positions is tied to organizational structure, not individual productivity.

title: Network and computer systems administrators
rationale: Cloud infrastructure and AI-managed systems automate much routine network and system administration. Infrastructure-as-code reduces manual configuration. Complex environments persist but fewer admins are needed per system.

title: News analysts, reporters, and journalists
rationale: AI generates routine news articles but investigative journalism and analysis require human judgment. Declining traditional media offset by growing digital and specialized news. Trust in human journalism provides some insulation.

title: Nuclear engineers
rationale: Niche field with demand tied to nuclear energy policy. Renewed interest in nuclear power (SMRs) and nuclear security may increase demand. AI assists with design and simulation but the field remains small.

title: Nuclear medicine technologists
rationale: Demand tied to nuclear medicine procedure volume, set by patient need and physician orders. AI aids image interpretation but human technologists must handle radioactive materials and operate equipment safely.

title: Nuclear technicians
rationale: Demand tied to nuclear facilities operations. Safety requirements maintain staffing levels. AI helps with monitoring but physical operations and safety protocols require human presence.

title: Nurse anesthetists, nurse midwives, and nurse practitioners
rationale: Major push to expand NP scope of practice to address physician shortages. Huge unmet demand for primary care and midwifery services. AI tools help with diagnosis and treatment planning while NPs provide the human care.

title: Nursing assistants and orderlies
rationale: Aging population creates massive demand for direct patient care. Physical caregiving strongly resists automation. Chronic staffing shortages indicate significant unmet demand. AI monitoring may improve care quality.

title: Occupational health and safety specialists and technicians
rationale: Demand tied to the number of workplaces and regulatory requirements. AI enables better monitoring but compliance requirements are set by regulation. New AI workplace safety concerns may expand the domain.

title: Occupational therapists
rationale: Significant unmet demand for rehabilitation and adaptive services. Aging population and growing awareness of developmental needs expand the patient pool. AI tools help create personalized treatment plans and monitor progress.

title: Occupational therapy assistants and aides
rationale: Hands-on therapeutic assistance resists automation. Growing demand from aging population and expanded OT services. AI tools may help extend the reach of each assistant.

title: Oil and gas workers
rationale: Long-term energy transition reduces fossil fuel demand. Automation and remote monitoring reduce field worker headcount. AI-optimized operations extract more with fewer workers. Cyclical commodity prices add volatility.

title: Operations research analysts
rationale: AI creates massive new optimization opportunities. Every logistics, scheduling, and resource allocation problem can benefit from OR techniques. AI tools make OR analysis feasible for more organizations and problems.

title: Opticians
rationale: Demand tied to vision correction needs in the population. Online eyewear sales provide some competition but fitting and adjustment require in-person service. Aging population supports demand.

title: Optometrists
rationale: Aging population increases vision care demand. AI diagnostic tools help optometrists detect disease earlier and more accurately. Some latent demand from people who don't get regular eye exams due to cost.

title: Orthotists and prosthetists
rationale: AI and 3D printing enable more personalized and affordable prosthetics and orthotics. Massive unmet demand globally, especially in developing countries. Technology makes custom devices accessible to more patients.

title: Painters, construction and maintenance
rationale: Physical painting in variable environments resists automation. Demand tied to construction and building maintenance. Some robotic painting emerges for large surfaces but interior and detail work persists.

title: Painting and coating workers
rationale: Industrial painting and coating is increasingly automated with robotic spraying systems. Demand tied to manufacturing volume. AI-guided quality control and robotic application reduce workers per production line.

title: Paralegals and legal assistants
rationale: AI automates much legal research, document review, and contract analysis. But expanding access to legal services (driven by AI efficiency) may create more paralegal work. Net slight reduction as routine tasks automate.

title: Personal financial advisors
rationale: Robo-advisors handle basic investment allocation, but complex financial planning and the trust relationship with clients persists. Growing wealth and retirement planning needs create demand. Middle-market advisory has latent demand.

title: Pest control workers
rationale: Physical pest control in varied environments resists automation. Demand tied to property stock and pest prevalence. AI-powered monitoring may improve targeting but application work needs humans.

title: Petroleum engineers
rationale: Long-term energy transition reduces demand for petroleum engineering. AI optimizes extraction but the industry is structurally declining. Some engineers transition to geothermal and carbon capture roles.

title: Pharmacists
rationale: Automated dispensing systems and AI drug interaction checking reduce the need for pharmacist oversight of routine prescriptions. Clinical pharmacy roles expand but retail pharmacy faces automation pressure. Net slight decline.

title: Pharmacy technicians
rationale: Automated pill counting, robotic dispensing, and digital prescription management directly reduce pharmacy technician tasks. Mail-order pharmacy further automates. Physical compounding persists but represents a small share.

title: Phlebotomists
rationale: Physical blood drawing resists automation (though robotic phlebotomy is in development). Demand tied to lab testing volume, which grows with aging population. AI has minimal current impact on the manual skill.

title: Photographers
rationale: AI image generation threatens stock photography but creates more demand for authentic human photography. Every business, event, and social media presence needs photography. Latent demand from businesses that couldn't afford professional photography.

title: Physical therapist assistants and aides
rationale: Hands-on therapeutic exercises resist automation. Aging population and growing PT demand increase needs. AI monitoring may help assistants serve more patients. Physical care cannot be delegated to AI.

title: Physical therapists
rationale: Significant unmet demand for physical therapy. Many patients are undertreated due to access and cost. AI tools help therapists create personalized programs and monitor progress remotely, extending reach to more patients.

title: Physician assistants
rationale: Massive unmet demand for primary and specialty care. PAs extend physician capacity and AI tools enhance their diagnostic capabilities. Growing scope of practice and acceptance. Healthcare access gaps indicate vast latent demand.

title: Physicians and surgeons
rationale: Enormous global unmet demand for medical care. AI diagnostic tools augment physician capabilities rather than replace them. Physicians become more effective with AI, potentially serving more patients and catching more conditions.

title: Physicists and astronomers
rationale: AI accelerates simulation and data analysis in physics. New research directions in quantum computing, fusion energy, and astrophysics. Research funding limits expansion more than productivity.

title: Plumbers, pipefitters, and steamfitters
rationale: Physical plumbing work in variable environments resists automation. Growing demand from aging infrastructure, water systems, and new construction. Persistent labor shortages indicate unmet demand.

title: Podiatrists
rationale: Demand tied to foot care needs in the population, growing modestly with aging and diabetes prevalence. AI diagnostics may help but the physical examination and treatment aspects persist.

title: Police and detectives
rationale: Public safety staffing is policy-driven and relatively stable per capita. AI aids surveillance and investigation but community policing requires human presence. Reform movements may alter staffing models in either direction.

title: Political scientists
rationale: AI enables more sophisticated political analysis and modeling. Growing demand for policy analysis, political risk assessment, and public opinion research. Think tanks and political consulting expand.

title: Postal service workers
rationale: Mail volume has been declining for decades as communication goes digital. AI-optimized sorting and autonomous delivery vehicles further reduce postal workforce needs. Package delivery grows but is increasingly automated.

title: Postsecondary education administrators
rationale: Administrative positions scale with the number of institutions and students. AI may automate some administrative tasks but regulatory compliance and student services persist. Enrollment trends are mixed.

title: Postsecondary teachers
rationale: Growing global demand for higher education. AI tools enhance teaching but cannot replace the mentorship, research guidance, and critical thinking development that professors provide. Online education expands access.

title: Power plant operators, distributors, and dispatchers
rationale: AI and automation increasingly manage grid operations and plant monitoring. The transition to distributed renewable energy changes the operator role. Fewer operators needed per unit of generation capacity.

title: Preschool and childcare center directors
rationale: Management positions scale with the number of childcare facilities. AI may help with administration but on-site leadership persists. Growing demand for childcare offsets efficiency gains.

title: Preschool teachers
rationale: Enormous unmet demand for quality early childhood education. Young children need human interaction and care. AI tools can help with individualized learning plans but cannot replace the teacher-child relationship.

title: Private detectives and investigators
rationale: AI tools enhance investigation capabilities (digital forensics, background checks) but also automate some research tasks. Growing cybersecurity and corporate fraud create new investigation demand.

title: Probation officers and correctional treatment specialists
rationale: Caseload driven by criminal justice system throughput, which is policy-dependent. AI risk assessment tools may alter supervision models. Reform movements may change demand in either direction.

title: Producers and directors
rationale: Explosion of content creation across streaming, social media, gaming, and corporate communications. AI tools assist production but creative vision and project leadership remain human. Every content platform needs more producers.

title: Project management specialists
rationale: Every organization runs projects, and AI enables more ambitious projects. AI automates scheduling and tracking but the human coordination and stakeholder management aspects persist. Growing project complexity maintains demand.

title: Property appraisers and assessors
rationale: AI and automated valuation models (AVMs) increasingly provide property value estimates. Many lenders accept AI-generated appraisals for standard properties. Complex and unique properties still need human assessment but standard appraisals automate.

title: Property, real estate, and community association managers
rationale: Management positions scale with the number of properties. AI helps with tenant communications and maintenance scheduling but on-site management and decision-making persist. Property stock grows modestly.

title: Psychiatric technicians and aides
rationale: Direct patient care in psychiatric settings resists automation. Growing mental health awareness and treatment access increase patient volume. Staffing shortages indicate unmet demand.

title: Psychologists
rationale: Enormous unmet demand for psychological services. Most people who could benefit from therapy don't receive it due to cost and access. AI tools can help psychologists screen, assess, and monitor more patients while maintaining the human therapeutic relationship.

title: Public relations and fundraising managers
rationale: Every organization needs reputation management, and the complexity of media channels grows. AI assists with monitoring and content creation but strategic communication and crisis management require human judgment.

title: Public relations specialists
rationale: Growing number of communication channels and stakeholders to manage. AI tools help with content creation and monitoring but relationship building and strategic messaging require human skills. Every organization needs PR.

title: Public safety telecommunicators
rationale: AI-assisted dispatch systems optimize routing and prioritization, reducing the number of human dispatchers needed. Computer-aided dispatch handles increasing volumes without proportional headcount increases.

title: Purchasing managers, buyers, and purchasing agents
rationale: AI automates supplier identification, price comparison, and routine procurement. E-procurement platforms reduce the need for purchasing intermediaries. Strategic procurement persists but transactional buying automates.

title: Quality control inspectors
rationale: AI-powered visual inspection and automated testing systems directly replace human quality inspectors on production lines. Machine vision outperforms humans in consistency and speed for many inspection tasks.

title: Radiation therapists
rationale: Demand tied to cancer patient volume receiving radiation therapy. AI improves treatment planning but human therapists must position patients and operate equipment. Patient volume grows modestly with cancer screening and aging.

title: Radiologic and MRI technologists
rationale: Demand tied to imaging order volume. AI improves image interpretation but human technologists must position patients and operate equipment. Growing imaging utilization supports demand while AI aids reading.

title: Railroad workers
rationale: Precision train control and automation reduce crew sizes. AI-managed scheduling and maintenance improve efficiency. Freight volume grows modestly but technology reduces workers per train-mile.

title: Real estate brokers and sales agents
rationale: Online listings and AI-powered property matching reduce the traditional agent role. iBuyer platforms and self-service tools disintermediate some transactions. Complex transactions still benefit from agents but standard sales shift to technology.

title: Receptionists
rationale: AI virtual receptionists, automated check-in kiosks, and digital scheduling directly replace routine reception tasks. Many offices already use automated phone systems and visitor management. The warm human greeting persists in some settings.

title: Recreation workers
rationale: Growing spending on leisure and wellness activities. Physical recreation programming requires human leadership. Community recreation programs have latent demand in underserved areas.

title: Recreational therapists
rationale: Growing recognition of therapeutic recreation for rehabilitation and mental health. Significant unmet need in aging populations and disability services. AI tools help personalize programs but the therapeutic relationship is human.

title: Registered nurses
rationale: Massive nursing shortage indicates enormous unmet demand. Aging population drives growing care needs. AI tools can help nurses manage more patients and catch issues earlier, but direct patient care requires human presence and compassion.

title: Rehabilitation counselors
rationale: Significant unmet demand for rehabilitation services. Many disabled individuals lack access to counseling. AI tools help counselors assess and monitor clients. Growing disability awareness and workplace accommodation needs expand demand.

title: Respiratory therapists
rationale: Aging population and chronic respiratory disease increase patient volume. AI assists with monitoring and treatment optimization but physical therapy delivery requires human practitioners. Pandemic awareness supports investment.

title: Retail sales workers
rationale: E-commerce continues to grow, reducing in-store sales positions. Self-checkout and AI-powered recommendation engines displace sales assistance. Experiential retail maintains some roles but overall headcount declines.

title: Roofers
rationale: Physical roofing work in variable conditions strongly resists automation. Demand tied to construction and re-roofing cycles. Climate change may increase storm damage repairs. Labor shortages indicate current unmet demand.

title: Sales engineers
rationale: Technical sales requires deep product knowledge and relationship building. AI helps with technical documentation and proposals but the consultative selling process persists. Demand tied to technical product markets.

title: Sales managers
rationale: Management roles scale with sales organization size. AI optimizes sales processes and provides better analytics but human leadership of sales teams persists. E-commerce growth shifts some sales management online.

title: School and career counselors and advisors
rationale: Significant unmet demand for student counseling—most schools have inadequate counselor-to-student ratios. AI tools help counselors serve more students with personalized guidance. Mental health awareness increases demand.

title: Secretaries and administrative assistants
rationale: AI scheduling tools, email management, and document preparation directly automate core secretarial tasks. Voice assistants and digital tools reduce the need for human administrative support. The role has been contracting for decades.

title: Securities, commodities, and financial services sales agents
rationale: Online trading platforms and robo-advisors reduce need for human brokers and agents. Algorithmic trading handles much of the transaction volume. Complex wealth management persists but standard financial product sales automate.

title: Security guards and gambling surveillance officers
rationale: AI surveillance systems, drones, and automated monitoring reduce the need for human guards. Technology handles surveillance while guards respond to incidents. Demand for physical security presence persists but monitoring shifts to AI.

title: Semiconductor processing technicians
rationale: Massive expansion of semiconductor manufacturing (CHIPS Act, AI chip demand) creates growing need for fabrication technicians. AI assists with process monitoring but cleanroom operations need human workers. Supply chain concerns drive domestic expansion.

title: Set and exhibit designers
rationale: Growing content production and experiential entertainment create demand. AI visualization tools help but physical design and construction of sets and exhibits requires human creativity and craftsmanship.

title: Sheet metal workers
rationale: Physical metalworking in varied environments resists automation. Demand tied to construction and HVAC activity. Growing demand for HVAC systems and building renovation supports the trade.

title: Skincare specialists
rationale: Growing consumer spending on skincare and wellness. Inherently physical, in-person service. AI skin analysis tools may expand client base by making consultations more accessible and personalized. Significant latent demand.

title: Small engine mechanics
rationale: Physical repair work resists automation. Demand tied to the installed base of small engines (mowers, generators, etc.). Transition to electric equipment may reduce long-term demand but the timeline is gradual.

title: Social and community service managers
rationale: Growing investment in social services and community programs. AI helps with administration and program evaluation but community leadership requires human connection. Expanding social safety net programs increase demand.

title: Social and human service assistants
